Full Statement: Kindergarten
The physically literate individual will demonstrate competency in a variety of motor skills and movement patterns.
Locomotor Skills
Locomotor (Hopping, galloping, running, sliding, skipping, leaping, walking, running)
Performs emerging patterns in locomotor skills (walk, run, leap, hop, gallop, slide, and skip) while maintaining balance (such as when you hear the color of your shirt leap over a pillow).
Perform mature patterns in locomotor skills (walk).
Locomotor (Jumping and landing in a horizontal and vertical plane)
Performs jumping and landing actions with balance (such as when you hear the color of your shirt, jump over a line on the floor).
Locomotor (Dance, Rhythm, Combinations)
Performs dance (rhythmic) activities in response to teacher led creative activities.
Non-Locomotor
Performs emerging patterns in nonlocomotor skills (such as bend, twist, turn, sway, stretch) in exploratory and a stable environment.
Non-Locomotor (Balance)
Maintains momentary balance (such as wide, narrow, curled and twisted body shapes) on different bases of support (such as walking on the floor).
Non-Locomotor (Weight Transfer)
Developmentally appropriate/emerging outcomes first appear in grade one.
Manipulative Skills

Throws underhand and overhand with opposite foot forward demonstrating an emerging pattern.
Manipulative Skills (Pass with Hands)

Dribbles a ball with one hand, attempting the second contact.

Demonstrates an emerging pattern while passing or kicking from a stationary position, demonstrating two of the five critical elements of a mature kicking pattern.
Manipulative Skills (Foot Dribble)
Soft taps a ball using the inside of the foot, sending it forward.
Manipulative Skills (Foot Trap Receive)
Performs emerging pattern while receiving with the preferred foot when stationary.
Manipulative Skills (Strike/Volley, Hands and Arms)
Volley a lightweight object (such as a balloon), sending it upward with an open palm.
